F1.evidence: local-workspace-projection-operation.ts:1600-1602 (diff) calls removeLocalWorkspaceCheckpointCapture unguarded in finally, so a throw there replaces run's result or error; prepareLocalWorkspaceCheckpointCapture (local-workspace-checkpoint.ts:1170) and the unchanged-probe path (local-workspace-projection.ts:1669) remove the leftover first and rethrow, so an unremovable checkpoint-capture fails every later checkpoint. fs-safe-copy.worker.ts remove only retries once after chmod repair and otherwise throws.

F2.evidence: With capture set, local-workspace-manifest-scan.ts:1452-1454 scans the snapshot root and workspace-actual-manifest.ts only treats ino 2 directories as incomplete, with no mount or device check, so a host-namespace bind mount (invisible to a btrfs snapshot) scans as an empty ordinary directory and its accepted files read as deleted; this needs an operator to bind-mount on the host inside a private projection, since guest container mounts are not visible to the Gateway's live scan either.

F3.evidence: fs-safe-copy.worker.ts prepareOwnedDirectoryRemoval skips chmod when (mode & 0o700) === 0o700 (a root-owned 0755 dir), so the second rmSync fails EACCES again for a non-root Gateway and the snapshot (which keeps guest ownership) stays; containers default to root (sandbox config user is optional, container-allocation.ts:106). This is a concrete trigger of the F1 cleanup failure that fails the accepted checkpoint and every later one.

F4.evidence: local-workspace-checkpoint.ts:1183-1190 (diff) does rethrow any copy error other than CLONE_UNAVAILABLE/EXDEV/ENOSYS instead of falling back to run(), but whether the native snapshot of a Gateway-owned subvolume fails with such errors under realistic conditions where the Git path would still succeed depends on the external @openclaw/fs-safe copyTree and host conditions, which are not in the repository.

F5.evidence: scripts/perf/local-workspace-checkpoint-measure.ts:2084-2086 enables accounting whenever /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.stat exists, and :2285 then reads /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max unguarded; cgroup v2 root has cpu.stat but no cpu.max, so a run without a cgroup namespace throws ENOENT while building the report. The doc (local-workspace-checkpoint-measure.md:42-43) asks for an exclusively owned cgroup, so this is a misconfigured-rig case.
